720	The head knows what is right and what is not,

right? For example, a person about to commit a sin

usually knows he is about to commit a sin. That is why

he looks right and left. Why? Because the mind

knows it is not good. But why does he commit

the sin? Because the heart craves. The heart has desire.

So if you are a king, with the mind ruling the heart, the mind

defeats the heart. But if you are Lemech, first craving,

then reason, then you are like the nations. So what does He

tell him? "And He will give their kings into your hand": everything that you call

their way, which is the way of Lemech, will be yours,

you will rule over it. Another thing:

Why does He give the kings? So you will know that if

the king falls,

the whole people falls after him, right? How did he make

his minister in heaven fall? The moment Moshe Rabbeinu saw the minister

of Og thrown down to the floor, he understood that they were already

losing. When something in heaven is cast to the floor, the whole

people will lose. The same here on earth. The people see the

king fall, all submit, they do not fight. How

do we know? In Yehoshua it is written, "And they brought out those kings

to Yehoshua." They won, they brought the kings

to Yehoshua. "And Yehoshua called all the men of Israel and said

to the chiefs of the men of war who went with him, come near, put

your feet on the necks of these kings." They made the

kings lie down, and all the officers of Israel put their

foot on their throats, which is the sign of humiliation and submission,

and it was fulfilled exactly as is written here: "and He will give their kings

into your hand." You see, exactly. Something He promised here

really happened.

What does He say now? He says: "The graven images of their gods

you shall burn with fire; you shall not covet the silver or the gold on them

and take it for yourself." Why? "Lest you be snared by it, for it is an abomination to HaShem

your Elokim." That is, you arrive and conquer

their village, there is plunder. Part of what they had was

statues of idol worship. Now what would they do? The statue he would make perhaps of wood

or stone, but he would adorn it with gold jewelry.

So He says: first of all, their statues you shall burn.

But what about the silver and gold? What a pity, there is silver and gold,

good, we could melt it down, maybe make rings

or bracelets for a woman, something. HaShem says: do not

covet the silver and gold on them. What is on the statues you must also

burn, destroy. Why? "Lest you be snared by it," like a mine. Even

if you melt it down, it will always nest in your head that it once

was idol worship, and maybe in the end it will make you fall

and you will worship through it somehow. So He says "lest you be snared." You might say,

"No, I am strong." You cannot be

strong, you do not know. There was once an inclination

for idol worship. Just as a man is forbidden to be alone with

a woman who is not his wife, in what is called yichud, so too

you do not know. Do not say "I am strong." There is no

guardian over lions, the Sages say. You do not know

how it will make you fall. The same with idol worship. Although

the Sages abolished the inclination for idol worship, we do not

understand that today, but once there was a very strong inclination

for idol worship. So He says you do not know

how it will make you fall, so you shall

utterly detest it. Why? "For it is an abomination to HaShem your Elokim."

"And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, lest you become accursed

like it. You shall utterly detest it and utterly abhor it, for it is accursed."

What does He say? Do not bring it into your house and do not bring in any

thing connected to idol worship into your house. Where does this

apply today? There are poor souls who do not know,

they come back from the East and bring statues of this Buddha,

what is he called? They bring statues of idol

worship like that. They put them in the house as decoration. All kinds of

things used for idol worship in the Far East, they put

these statues of this Buddha, and they think it is decoration, but it is idol worship.

Do not bring idol worship into your house. So wait, a person

will say, what is the problem? Do I bow to it? Do I

worship it? It is just decoration. Tell me, if now

the police come to someone's house, search it, and find

a machine for printing dollars,

he says, "But I did not print any dollars, I only

keep the machine." Ah, they will say, fine then, you are

fine, great, of course! Or a lab,

equipment, a lab for producing drugs, he says, "But I did not

produce drugs." But sir, you have prohibited equipment here.

So you see, even if you did not commit

the offense, the very fact that you keep the tools for committing

the offense, you will be seized for that in court too, right?

The same here: you bring idol worship home, you

say, "But I did not worship," so what is it doing at your

house? So whoever did not know, poor fellow, that is why

we hear a Torah class. It is worthwhile for everyone to go through the house,

check whether he has something resembling idol worship, all

kinds of statues, all kinds of unrelated things, throw them out of

the house. Why do you need it, so that on the Day of Judgment

you will give an account for such a thing? May HaShem have mercy. Some

say "do not bring an abomination into your house" refers to the woman

of beautiful form: if you go to war and see a beautiful

gentile woman, even though the Torah, under very, very, very,

very strict conditions, permitted her to you,

it says do not bring the abomination into your house.

Now what else is "do not bring an abomination into your house,

and you will be cherem like it"? Cherem has the letters of chomer, right,

without the vav: that you not be far from HaShem, with matter,

with materialism without spirituality. For what is cherem? Cherem is

matter; matter distances you from HaShem. Cherem is also the

letters of Ramach: if you bring an abomination, it will bring

troubles on your 248 limbs. Cherem is also the letters of rachem:

whoever repents and throws it out

of the house, HaShem has mercy on him. So you see how many

hints. Now what else does He tell him? "All the commandment which

I command you today you shall observe to do, that you may live,

and multiply, and go in and possess the land which HaShem swore

to your fathers." That is, what does He say to him?

"That you may live and multiply." That is, see, the Torah

is a Torah of life, and HaKadosh Baruch Hu promises

that keeping the mitzvot brings a person vitality. Wait, but

someone will say, wait, I know some who

keep nothing, and they are alive. I know one who commits

every sin, eats pork, eats this,

desecrates Shabbatot, and lives, right? He is physically alive like

a cow, like a dog, a dog is also alive, a cow is also alive. But

what? They are alive physically, but he has no spiritual

vitality. Vitality is a spiritual matter, and it continues

afterward into the World to Come. Woe to whoever comes
